key_insight: Temperature-dependent Raman and XRD can separate a low-temperature octahedral distortion from a higher-temperature symmetry-breaking phase transition in SrLaCoNbO6.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical, lab-based diagnostic workflow for tracking structure-property changes in ordered double perovskites relevant to functional oxide and solar-cell materials screening.
method: Combined Raman spectroscopy and laboratory XRD from 25–900 °C
Tracked phonon frequency/linewidth renormalization and reflection evolution
Quantified octahedral distortion parameters with structural refinement and group theory
evidence_signal: Two clear anomalies were observed at T_OD = 300 ± 25 °C and T_PT = 750 ± 25 °C, with correlated phonon changes and disappearance/evolution of XRD peaks supporting the assigned structural changes.
watch_item: The temperature thresholds are approximate and the structural assignments rely on lab-based diffraction and vibrational analysis, so subtle intermediate phases could be missed without higher-resolution methods.
paper_title: Disentangling octahedral distortion and symmetry breaking in the ordered double perovskite SrLaCoNbO$_6$
